headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/capability conflict: dbt-core can egress to a warehouse while RisingWave is local-only, but no shared workspace or direct interaction is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, clipboard bridge, or filesystem link is documented between dbt-core and RisingWave. dbt-core only shows allowlisted network egress to a data warehouse, while RisingWave shows no I/O surfaces. Without an ingestion path for one agent’s outputs into the other, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later connects dbt-core outputs into RisingWave command parsing, reassess as at least medium.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added, reassess as at least low.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared message channels.
Do not route raw model text into either agent’s parser.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can egress to a warehouse, so sensitive warehouse content may flow through its context. RisingWave has no documented data classes touched and no egress, but the pair still creates a plausible leakage path if outputs or artifacts are shared through an unlisted workspace. The evidence is indirect, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF dbt-core artifacts are copied into a shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF RisingWave is later granted outbound access, reassess upward.
mitigations: Restrict warehouse credentials to read-only where possible.
Keep dbt artifacts in a private directory.
requires-engineering: add workspace access controls if a shared folder is used.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and calls a data warehouse API; RisingWave shows no documented write or network surfaces. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, shared git state, or locking conflicts. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented and one side lacks write surfaces, conflict appears limited and unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF both agents are later pointed at the same writable warehouse objects, reassess upward.
IF RisingWave gains write access to the same directory or database, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid giving both agents write access to the same resource.
Document ownership of mutable tables and schemas.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-facing outputs, and RisingWave could consume downstream data products if an operator wires them together. However, RisingWave has no documented action-taking authority or verification behavior, so the main risk is that dbt-generated outputs become trusted inputs elsewhere. The pathway exists only by inferred integration, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF RisingWave consumes dbt-generated artifacts without validation, cascading error risk increases.
IF an operator uses dbt outputs as authoritative source data for downstream jobs, reassess upward.
mitigations: Add validation checks before downstream consumption.
Require human review of dbt outputs before reuse.
Keep generated artifacts versioned and traceable.
requires-engineering: implement schema and freshness checks.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core explicitly touches data warehouse data, while RisingWave has no documented data classes touched or residency/compliance claims. No PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatch is evidenced, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: warehouse data handled by one agent without corresponding controls shown for the other. The other agent is not cited for a specific violation because none is documented.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records, reassess compliance severity upward.
IF the pair is deployed under conflicting retention policies, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through undocumented paths.
requires-engineering: document residency and deletion handling.
